clue.text: Optimistic European, one inclined to go north

definitions.note: the north-seeking end of a magnet, the one a compass needle swings towards the north

parts.note: an optimistic outlook is a positive one
a Pole is a native of Poland, a European

explanation.surface: A cheerful traveller from Europe who likes heading north for holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the magnet: its positive end is the one that points, or 'is inclined', north.
explanation.definitionFit: In a magnet the north-seeking end is called the positive end, so it is the end tending northwards.

clue.text: Hair and metallic thread upsettingly swallowed by farm animal

indicators.note: something swallowed by another ends up inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a pig is a farm animal

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting turns a word upside down, so its letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: wire is a thread of metal

explanation.surface: A grim farmyard mishap: a pig gulps down someone's hairpiece and a length of wire.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upsettingly' means read from bottom to top; 'Hair' here is a wig, false hair, not hair that grows.
explanation.definitionFit: A periwig is an old-fashioned wig, false hair worn by gentlemen and lawyers.

clue.text: This person's entertained by boy, simple lad?

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is held within the host's home, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a son is a boy
the setter speaking of themself: this person is = I am, contracted

explanation.surface: The setter is being hosted by a boy who seems a bit slow.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to Simple Simon of the nursery rhyme, who met a pieman on his way to the fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple Simon is the foolish youngster of the English nursery rhyme, hence a simple-minded lad's name.

clue.text: Woman with shots going round hides in these workplaces

indicators.note: one piece circling another surrounds it, so the other sits within

parts.note: a shot is an attempt or try
Anne is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman surrounded by gunfire hides away inside some workshops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hides' looks like a verb, someone ducking for cover; it is the noun, animal skins, which these workplaces treat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tannery is a works where animal skins are cured and turned into leather.

clue.text: Prohibit nothing after check

indicators.note: the word for nothing is placed after the word for check

parts.note: to vet is to check or examine
O, the round figure zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: An instruction to ban nothing once something has been inspected.
explanation.definitionFit: A veto is an official refusal, so to veto a measure is to forbid it.

clue.text: Private agent set up new salon

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means raised, so the word is read upwards

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is a sales agent

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters of salon

explanation.surface: An agent works privately to open a new beauty salon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns REP into PER; 'new' rearranges SALON as SONAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Personal and private both describe matters belonging to one individual and not shared.

clue.text: Secures hair

definitions.meaning: fastens shut with a key, as a door
tresses or curls of a person's hair

explanation.surface: Someone fastens their hair in place.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both fastens with a bolt and tresses, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Fresh role — go up giving introduction to play

indicators.note: fresh signals that the letters of role, go and up are given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An actor with a new part rises to deliver the play's opening speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' looks like it describes the role, but it rearranges all of ROLE, GO and UP together.
explanation.definitionFit: A prologue is the opening speech or section that introduces a drama.

clue.text: Composer to manage being heard

indicators.note: being heard means the word is judged by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: to handle a matter is to manage it

explanation.surface: A composer struggles to cope with having his music listened to.
explanation.walkthrough: George Frideric Handel, composer of Messiah.
explanation.definitionFit: Handel was the German-born Baroque composer who worked in London.

clue.text: What's odd in a politician, almost the thinker?

parts.note: rum is old British slang for odd or strange

indicators.note: almost means not quite the whole word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A question asking what is strange about a politician who is nearly the deep thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruminator is one who mulls things over at length, a pondering thinker.

clue.text: Scoundrel, one brought before a church court

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible scoundrel
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A rogue, someone, is hauled before an ecclesiastical tribunal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Curia is the papal court and administration of the Roman Catholic Church.

clue.text: Like escaped criminal worker caught during day

indicators.note: something caught during another is held within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Wed is the short form of Wednesday
a worker ant is the crossword's usual worker

explanation.surface: A labourer is nabbed one day, rather like a fugitive.
explanation.definitionFit: A criminal on the run is sought by the police, as on a poster headed with that word.

clue.text: Prisoners stuck in 'ollow place must be sympathised with

parts.note: cons, short for convicts, are prisoners
holed, stuck in a hole, with its h dropped as the apostrophe in 'ollow signals

explanation.surface: Prisoners trapped in a cavity deserve our pity, said in a dropped-aitch accent.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophes mark the dropped h of Cockney speech: 'ollow is hollow, so a hollow place is an 'ole and being stuck in it is 'OLED.
explanation.definitionFit: To console someone is to comfort them in grief, so consoled means comforted or sympathised with.

clue.text: Try and be still, hugging a player on the field

indicators.note: the two words wrap around the letter between them as arms hug a body

parts.note: a go is a try or attempt
to lie is to stay still, as lying low

explanation.surface: Advice to a sportsman to have a go and keep still while embracing a teammate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hugging' applies to the pair joined by 'and': together they wrap around the A.
explanation.definitionFit: A goalkeeper, informally so called, is a team member on the pitch in football or hockey.

clue.text: Planned a road to bypass mountains

indicators.note: a road bypassing something goes around it, so it encloses the other piece

parts.note: a range is a chain of mountains

explanation.surface: Engineers have designed a highway that skirts a mountain chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Something arranged has been organised in advance, so it is planned.

clue.text: Insane trick by Jolson in song

parts.note: mad means insane
to rig is to fix by trickery, and a rig is a trick
Al Jolson was the American singer of The Jazz Singer

explanation.surface: A crazy stunt by the old entertainer Al Jolson during a number.
explanation.definitionFit: A madrigal is a part-song for several unaccompanied voices, popular in Renaissance times.

clue.text: Introduce woeful cut

indicators.note: woeful means dreadfully bad, so the letters of introduce are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone is bringing in a miserable pay cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Introduce' looks like an instruction but is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A reduction is a lowering or decrease, such as a cut in price or spending.

clue.text: Bearing of one in anger following vehicle

indicators.note: the anger part comes after the vehicle word

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the word for anger

parts.note: rage is fierce anger
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A furious person's posture behind the wheel of a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing' looks like a machine part or a compass direction, but it is the way a person holds themself.
explanation.definitionFit: Carriage is the way one holds oneself, one's deportment or posture.

clue.text: Identifies fellow as one likely to hit target

parts.note: to mark out is to identify or single out
a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: Someone picks out a chap who looks a good shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A marksman is a skilled shooter, so one expected to hit what he aims at.

clue.text: Trouble created by furry creature on street

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: a mole is a small furry burrowing animal

explanation.surface: A burrowing animal on the road causes a disturbance.
explanation.definitionFit: To molest is to pester or harass, an old sense of troubling someone.

clue.text: Coming ahead of the festive season

definitions.meaning: an arrival, the coming of something
the church season of the four weeks before Christmas

explanation.surface: Something arriving just before Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an arrival in general and the period of preparation leading up to Christmas.

clue.text: There is time for those not yet considered

parts.note: contracted to there's

explanation.surface: A reassurance that there will be time to deal with the remaining items.
explanation.definitionFit: The remaining ones, the others still to be dealt with, are the leftover people or things.

clue.text: Letter to settle status of ennobled man

parts.note: to land is to come down and settle, as a bird does
a man made a peer takes the rank of lord

explanation.surface: A written message deciding the rank of a newly made peer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' looks like a written message or a character of the alphabet, but it means one who lets property to tenants.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lets a house or flat to tenants is the owner renting it out.

clue.text: Words coming from Heather with love

parts.note: ling is a common name for heather
love is nil in tennis, the round figure O

explanation.surface: Affectionate words from a woman called Heather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name but is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A lingo is a language or jargon, the words a group uses.

clue.text: Graze a bit, needing energy

parts.note: a scrap is a small piece or bit
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A minor cut that requires some vigour to recover from.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrape is a shallow skin injury, the same as a graze.

clue.text: No. 51 in avenue becomes animated

indicators.note: the number goes inside the abbreviation for avenue

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A house at number 51 on an avenue comes to life.
explanation.definitionFit: Being lively and full of energy is a figurative sense of being living.

clue.text: Work up and down in part of ship

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
the same abbreviation for work, now read downwards

explanation.surface: Someone toils up and down on the deck of a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: The one word for work gives OP twice: read up it is PO, read down it is OP.
explanation.definitionFit: The poop is the raised deck at the stern of a sailing ship.

clue.text: Back being tough

explanation.surface: A firm stance at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the rear part of a boat and severe or strict.

clue.text: Native — one getting drink in a hole in the ground?

indicators.note: the numeral and the drink go inside the hole

parts.note: a bore is a hole drilled into the ground, as for water
I is the Roman numeral for one
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: A local takes a drink while sitting in a pit.
explanation.definitionFit: An Aborigine is one of the original inhabitants of Australia, a native people.

clue.text: Adulterer agreeing to lose one of two rights

indicators.note: of the pair of letters for rights, one is dropped

parts.note: corresponding things agree, so the matching word is one in agreement
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: An unfaithful spouse, in accord with dropping one of a pair of entitlements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rights' means R's: CORRESPONDENT has two, and 'to lose one of two rights' drops one.
explanation.definitionFit: In a divorce case the co-respondent is the person cited as having committed adultery with the spouse.
